text:
maria: Heads up — CI alerts showed 3x OOM spikes 02:12->02:40 UTC on prod-serving. Dump attached: s3://redwood-prod-profiler/2768123456/dump.pb.gz. Quick read: KV prefill rate doubled, lots of tiny allocations, slab fragmentation.

zane: I saw that. Prefill canonicalizer seems to create duplicate keys when prompt sanitization hits non-ascii. Example: `prompt.normalize()` -> key_hash mismatch. We have both `k:abc` and `k:%E2%...` in cache which defeats dedupe.

sam: Does kernel selection worsen this? If KV entries vary in length, batching might pick larger kernel and pad, increasing memory footprint and scratch allocations.

maria: Yes — profiler shows frequent kernel-switch at 128->512 sequence boundary. ~20% of batches are flipping to the 512 kernel which uses ~2.3x more intermediate buffers.

lee: Short-term mitigation: ramp TTL down for low-hit cohorts and favor aggressive LRU for GPU slab to free small fragments faster. Proposed tweak: 
```
cache.tiers.gpu.default_ttl=60
cache.tiers.gpu.low_hit_ttl=15
cache.eviction.strategy=prob-lru
```
This should reduce resident tiny-allocs while we fix canonicalization.

clair: I'll open PR for canonicalization in the prefill path: steps = normalize -> NFC -> remove-zero-width -> utf8-escape -> stable-hash. That should collapse dup keys and keep hit-rate stable.

zane: Can we also make kernel selection more stable? Current rule flips on per-batch median seq; if we instead use percentile-based sticky rules (e.g., keep using 128 kernel unless >30% of requests >256) we can avoid oscillation and padding churn.

sam: Yes — plus add a short hysteresis window (60s) for kernel decision so we don't thrash during traffic bursts. Also add a sampling profiler for kernel-flip-rate and alloc-per-batch metrics. Alert when flip-rate >5%/min.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: deployment started for patch/ttl-tweak by lee at 2026-03-18T09:23Z

maria: Initial post-deploy telemetry: OOMs dropped ~80% in first hour, 95th latency unchanged, hit-rate roughly stable. Heap fragmentation metric down ~30% but still above baseline. Need 24h to validate. Action items: clair to PR canonicalizer; zane to prototype percentile sticky kernel policy; sam to add kernel-flip-rate metric and alert.

lee: I'll keep the TTL change live for 24h, will rollback if error/latency/regressions show. Leaving a note: link to dashboard: https://console.redwood/metrics/cache/2768123456. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — filing a short postmortem if we still see residual fragmentation after canonicalization.
